I will keep cotton as my main crop because that is the crop system I know best and it fits my land and my years of experience. At the start of the season, I will spread my 16.9 mu so the farm is not too risky: I will put the biggest share into cotton, keep some winter wheat for grain and income stability, plant some maize because it is reliable and useful for the household, and keep a smaller area of mungbean because it needs less water and fertilizer and helps spread labor. Since some family members work off-farm, I will not choose a plan that needs too much fine management every day. I have well irrigation, so I will use it where it matters most, especially for cotton, wheat, and maize at key stages. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and stand establishment, but I will keep inputs moderate because I farm for steady returns, not for the highest possible spending. I will plough for cotton and wheat because I want a clean seedbed, use rotary tillage for maize, and keep mungbean simpler. I will use fertilizer more heavily on wheat, maize, and cotton, and less on mungbean. I will spray pesticides when needed, with more attention on cotton because insects are usually a bigger problem there. This is the plan I would follow for my own farm this year.
